title: Fill a Grid in a Spiral
statement:
Given a size n, build an n × n grid and write the numbers 1, 2, …, n² into it along a clockwise spiral.

Start in the top-left cell and go right along the top row. Whenever the next cell is outside the grid or already filled, turn right (clockwise) and keep going. Return the filled grid as a list of rows.

examples.why: Right along the top, down the right edge, left along the bottom, up the left edge, then the single centre cell.
After the outer ring ends at 12, the walk turns right again and goes clockwise around the inner 2 × 2 block: 13, 14, 15, 16.

hints: Simulate the walk: keep a position and a direction, and know when to turn.
Turn when the next cell is off the grid or already has a number. Directions cycle right, down, left, up.
Or peel layers: keep top, bottom, left and right bounds, fill the four sides of the current ring, then shrink all four bounds by one.

explain.intuition:
This is the reverse of reading a grid in spiral order, and the same two techniques work. The first is pure simulation: walk, write the next number, and turn clockwise when you would run off the edge or into a cell you already filled. Since you are building the grid, "already filled" is just "not zero".

The second peels the grid ring by ring. Keep four bounds. Fill the top row from left to right, then the right column downward, then the bottom row leftward, then the left column upward, and move each bound one step inward. Because the grid is square, the last ring is either a 2 × 2 block or a single centre cell, and the bounds handle both.
steps: Create an n × n grid of zeros and set top = 0, bottom = n − 1, left = 0, right = n − 1, next = 1.
While top ≤ bottom and left ≤ right: fill grid[top][left..right], then increase top.
If rows remain, fill grid[bottom][right..left] and decrease bottom; if columns remain, fill grid[bottom..top][left] and increase left.
pitfalls: Filling a ring's corners twice by letting every side run its full length. Each side must start one cell after the previous side ended.
Skipping the bounds check before the bottom and left sides. On odd n the centre cell would be written twice.
Turning counter-clockwise: after the top row comes the right column, going down.

solutions.title: Walk and turn
solutions.idea: Simulate the walk with a direction vector. Turn clockwise whenever the next cell is outside the grid or already filled.

solutions.title: Peel ring by ring
solutions.idea: Keep four bounds. Fill the top, right, bottom and left sides of the current ring and shrink the bounds.

followups: Fill an m × n rectangle instead of a square. Which bounds checks start to matter?
Without building the grid, compute which number lands in cell (r, c).
